kid.question: What does the Lord say will stand?

options.text: Babylon’s throne
His counsel
A carved image
The astrologers’ charts

kid.explanation: The Lord alone declares the end from the beginning, and His counsel stands.

kid.question: What does the Lord promise to bring near?

options.text: A wooden idol
Babylon’s throne
His salvation
A new prison

kid.explanation: The Lord calls an agent from afar and promises to bring salvation near despite the hearers’ stubbornness.

kid.question: What happens to Babylon’s throne in Isaiah 47?

options.text: It becomes higher
It turns to gold
It is moved to Zion
She loses it

kid.explanation: Babylon is called down from her throne to the dust and loses the title “lady of kingdoms.”

kid.question: How did Babylon treat the people placed in its hand?

options.text: Without mercy
With gentle care
As honored guests
As free rulers

kid.explanation: Babylon showed no mercy to the Lord’s people and acted as though its rule would last forever.

kid.question: What does Babylon wrongly say about its wrongdoing?

options.text: I need forgiveness
No one sees me
I will restore the captives
I have listened to Isaiah

kid.explanation: Babylon’s hidden wickedness and reliance on its own wisdom cannot prevent sudden disaster.

kid.question: Can Babylon’s stargazers save it?

options.text: Yes, by reading the stars
Yes, by buying gold
No

kid.explanation: Astrologers and other advisers cannot save Babylon; they scatter as its judgment arrives.

kid.question: Why did the Lord announce things before they happened?

options.text: So Israel could avoid listening
So Babylon could build an image
So people could forget the events
So idols could not claim the credit

kid.explanation: Israel invokes the Lord’s name without truth, and the Lord announced events beforehand so idols could not receive credit.

kid.question: Why does the Lord tell Israel new things?

options.text: So they can recognize His work
So they can praise an idol
So they can hide the past
So they can stop listening

kid.explanation: The Lord reveals new things so Israel cannot claim it already knew them, despite its closed ears.

kid.question: What image describes Israel’s hardship?

options.text: A road of flowers
A furnace of affliction
A gold throne
A river of peace

kid.explanation: The Lord delays anger and refines Israel in affliction for His name’s sake.

kid.question: Who laid the foundation of the earth in this passage?

options.text: Babylon
An astrologer
The Lord
A carved image

kid.explanation: The Lord calls Himself first and last, creator of earth and heavens, and summons people to hear His purpose for Babylon.
